articles.title: BBC Women's Football Weekly - Ruthless England advance in World Cup play-offs - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: After two standout displays, has Le Tissier made a case to start alongside Bronze?
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 13 Oct 2026 , · 30 mins

Katie Smith is joined by former England goalkeeper, Rachel Brown-Finnis, and 5 Live commentator Vicki Sparks to react to England’s 5-0 win (8-1 on aggregate) over Greece which sees them progress to round two of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs. After lacking a clinical edge in the first-leg, the Lionesses were far more ruthless at home, plus we saw two more debuts for Lexi Potter and Freya Godfrey. The team discuss whether Sarina Wiegman has become more tactically flexible when it comes to her starting XI and whether Maya Le Tissier’s standout performances at right-back have posed the question: can both she and Lucy Bronze start for the national team? Plus, Rob Schofield is down in the tunnel to get reaction from Alessia Russo, Grace Fisk and Sarina Wiegman. TIMECODES: 00:05 - Reaction to a more ruthless England performance. 06:50 - Alessia Russo interview 08:40 - Lexi Potter’s debut and Sarina Wiegman making more changes to her starting XI. 17:20 - Grace Fisk interview. 19:35 - Should Maya Le Tissier and Lucy Bronze play together for England? 25:20 - Sarina Wiegman interview.

articles.summary:

articles.title: CNN All Access will give streaming cable news another try, for $6.99 a month
articles.summary: Over three years after it shut down CNN Plus, CNN All Access launches on October 28th with more content and an introductory launch promotion.
articles.body: CNN has announced a new subscription service called All Access that will launch in the US on October 28th, 2025. It will cost $6.99 per month, or $69.99 annually, with a special introductory price of $41.99 for the first year for those who sign up by January 5th, 2026. Plans for the new subscription were first revealed in an internal company memo from CNN CEO Mark Thompson that was shared with The Verge earlier this year. The All Access tier will include access to a selection of CNN’s US and international live programming, but like the short-lived CNN Plus that was shut down a month after launching, it doesn’t include a live feed of CNN’s cable news channel. But All Access offers more than the $5.99 per month CNN Plus did, including over 1,000 hours of content from the CNN Originals library, video-on-demand content, exclusive live events, and the “latest CNN Original Series and CNN Films” – but those will only be available the day after they air on TV. It will also include access to all of the articles and subscriber-only content on CNN.com. CNN says “current Pay TV subscribers” will have access to All Access at no additional cost, but without access to the articles on CNN.com. The website can be accessed through CNN’s existing digital subscription, which launched last October as the rebranded $3.99/month Basic tier.

articles.title: Peacock is adding an AI Andy Cohen to narrate an endless stream of Bravo clips
articles.summary: Peacock is adding an endless stream of clips from Bravo series, narrated by the AI likeness of TV host Andy Cohen.
articles.body: When you open your Peacock mobile app this summer, you might see a portal leading to the AI likeness of TV host Andy Cohen on your homepage. In an announcement on Friday, NBCUniversal said Cohen’s avatar will serve as a guide through Peacock’s “infinitely swipeable” feed of clips from Bravo shows, like Love Island, The Real Housewives series, and Below Deck. The feed, called “Your Bravoverse,” will surface clips from the shows that you choose when you first open up the new experience. NBCUniversal will use AI to scan and pick out scenes from your favorite shows, while an AI-generated Cohen offers input about what’s happening on screen. [Video: Peacock Bravoverse] Peacock’s short-form video expansion is part of a broader trend that has streaming services trying to keep viewers locked into their apps. This week, Disney Plus followed ESPN by adding a new stream of clips, called “verts,” while Netflix has also experimented with a short-form feed. John Jelley, NBCUniversal’s senior vice president of product, told reporters that with the use of AI, the company can create 600 billion different variations of the Bravoverse feed. “We’ve used AI and an AI agent that we’ve trained on what Bravo fans care about,” Jelley said. “There might be tens of thousands of clips and moments and metadata, but we know that fans love an explosive walk-out.” [Image: Law & Order: Clue Hunter launches on Peacock in the spring. A short-form video feed isn’t Peacock’s only play to capture user attention; it’s also adding a new Law & Order: Clue Hunter mobile game this spring. The game comes from Wolf Games, the AI-enabled studio cofounded by Elliot Wolf, the son of Law & Order creator Dick Wolf. It asks users “to find hidden objects to help identify suspects and solve a mystery,” according to the press release. Peacock is also adding Public Eye to its app this summer, another title from Wolf Games that uses AI to generate a new mystery to solve each day. Disclosure: Comcast, which owns NBCUniversal, is also an investor in Vox Media, The Verge’s parent company. Update, March 13th: Clarified the presence of the Bravoverse on Peacock’s homepage.

articles.title: Google is testing AI chatbot search for YouTube
articles.summary: Google is trying out an AI Mode-like search called “Ask YouTube” that builds a result page with videos, Shorts, and text.
articles.body: Google is trying out an AI Mode-like search experience for YouTube. The company is now testing “a new way to search on YouTube that feels more like a conversation,” with results pulling in things like longform videos, YouTube Shorts, and text about what you’re searching for. The “experiment” is now available if you’re a YouTube Premium subscriber in the US who is 18 or older. I turned it on for my account. Now, in the search bar, I see an “Ask YouTube” button, and clicking the search bar shows prompts to ask like “funny baby elephant playing clips,” “summary of the rules of volleyball,” and “short history of the Apollo 11 moon landing.” If I keep the search box blank but click the Ask YouTube button, YouTube takes me to a full page with suggested searches and a text box to ask a question. [Image: When you search with Ask YouTube, YouTube briefly shows a mostly blank page with a loading icon, and after a few seconds, fills it out with text and details. I tested it with the “short history of the Apollo 11 moon landing” prompt. At the top of the results was a bunch of text summarizing the mission, including a bulleted list of milestones like the date of the lunar landing and Neil Armstrong’s first step on the Moon. Then, the page included a video about the launch timestamped to a section about the launch day from a channel called “The Life Guide,” followed by galleries of videos under headers like “From Launch to Splashdown,” “Historic Footage and Behind-the-Scenes,” and a series of Shorts about “Moments on the Surface.” (I assume YouTube is pulling the text for these sections from the videos highlighted in the search results.) At the end, the page has a few more suggested prompts, including “Who were the Apollo 11 astronauts” and (perhaps worryingly) “Apollo 11 conspiracy theories,” and a text box I can use to ask a follow-up question or start a new search. I clicked the “Who were the Apollo 11 astronauts” and got a new, slightly differently formatted set of results, including a grid with background about astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins. Searching for “Apollo 11 conspiracy theories” just showed a typical list of YouTube search results, however. [Image: I threw Ask YouTube another test to see how it fared with something I’m very familiar with: Valve’s new Steam Controller, which I published a review of today. I asked, “What is the Steam Controller,” and YouTube gave an overview of the controller, pointed to Valve’s new video about the controller, and highlighted both longform reviews and a “Quick Hands-On Reviews” section featuring Shorts (including our new Short published today and one from last November). [Image: The second and fourth Shorts are The Verge’s. It was all mostly right, but I did catch a factual flub: YouTube claimed that the old, discontinued Steam Controller had no joysticks, when it actually has one. It was a reminder that, as potentially useful as these AI-created search result pages might seem, you need to do your due diligence to make sure they’re accurate. YouTube says it’s already “working on” expanding this experiment to users who don’t have Premium. Just as it’s continued to iterate on AI Mode and brought AI Mode to Gmail, it seems likely that “Ask YouTube” is something Google sees a big future for.

articles.title: Bills vs. Rams live updates, inactives, where to watch: DJ Moore inactive as Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford face off in potential Super Bowl LXI preview
articles.summary: The Rams and Bills will close out Week 5 on "Monday Night Football."
articles.body: The Buffalo Bills head west to close out Week 5 against the Los Angeles Rams on “Monday Night Football,” with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium.Despite a 2-2 start, the Rams remain the favorites to win Super Bowl LXI at +600 on FanDuel Sportsbook, with the 3-1 Bills not far behind at +850. Those odds tell only part of the story heading into Monday’s finale, which could very well be a preview of this season’s Super Bowl, a showdown between the last two NFL MVPs in Josh Allen (2024) and Matthew Stafford (2025).The Bills will be without one of their top receiving weapons in Week 5, with wideout DJ Moore inactive due to a shoulder injury he aggravated in last week’s loss to the New England Patriots, along with WR Joshua Palmer. The Rams, meanwhile, will have All-Pro defensive tackle Aaron Donald available after missing last week with back soreness. None of those news items should considered a positive for Allen, with the Bills already 3.5-point road underdogs Monday night.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Rams host the Bills to close out Week 5 on “Monday Night Football,” airing on ESPN.

articles.title: Dodgers vs. Brewers score, live updates: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Logan Henderson take the mound in Game 2 of NLCS
articles.summary: The Brewers took Game 1 of the NLCS with a 2-1 win over the Dodgers on Sunday.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are back in action on Monday for Game 2 of the NLCS at American Family Field in Milwaukee, with first pitch set for 5 p.m. ET. After getting swept by the Dodgers in last year's NLCS, the Brewers came out with a 2-1 win in Game 1, with Los Angeles' offense looking vulnerable as it continues to struggle to produce hits with runners in scoring position.The Dodgers will deploy another ace Monday, following Game 1's start from Tarik Skubal with right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9, 2.53 ERA) on the mound. Yamamoto's lone start of this postseason came in Game 3 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves, and he struck out 10 while giving up four hits and one earned run over seven innings.The Brewers will start right-hander Logan Henderson (11-3, 2.47 ERA) in Game 2. He most recently started Game 2 of the NLDS against the San Diego Padres, a 4-3 win thanks to some late-game heroics from outfielder Jackson Chourio. Henderson pitched five innings in that game, striking out 4 and walking 3 while allowing 2 runs (1 earned). Left-handed hitters Christian Yelich, Sal Frelick and David Hamilton are all back in the lineup in Game 2 after sitting against left-hander Skubal in Game 1. Yelich and Frelick both scored on Chourio's walk-off single in Game 2 of the NLDS.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Brewers host the Dodgers in Game 2 of the NLCS, airing on Fox.

articles.title: WWE Raw results, grades (Oct. 12): Carmelo Hayes joins 946 for brutal Bloodline beatdown
articles.summary: The latest "WWE Raw" followed up Money in the Bank with a big-time angle in the main event — and a noteworthy return.
articles.body: "WWE Raw" was in Bossier City, Louisiana at the Brookshire Grocery Arena on this Monday, Oct. 12. After an eventful Money in the Bank 2026 went down in New Orleans, the red brand followed it up with a big-time angle in the main event — along with a noteworthy return.He's alive!No, unfortunately, this isn't an update on Jacob Fatu, who’s somewhat hilariously been a complete afterthought by the entire WWE since Jaida Parker's vehicular murder attempt.Instead, I'm referring to Carmelo Hayes, who is not only back on our screens, but he's on "Raw" and has joined the 946.CARMELO HAYES!!!! 😱😱😱 pic.twitter.com/nm02fTN6h1— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 A week or two ago, I thought about how ridiculous it was for Hayes to disappear (again) after his latest U.S. Title pursuits on "SmackDown." His alliance with The 946 is random on the surface, but it's extremely refreshing for him. Presumably, his poor booking and getting left in the dust will be used as his reasoning for wanting to prove a point and join this squad, which is fair — if that's the case. Either way, I can't complain, as he deserves a main-event-caliber spotlight after the great work he did pre-WrestleMania.Hayes is a unique addition to the trio of big men (plus Parker), since he's the smaller, high-flyer type, while still being jacked in his own right. Really, that makes him an awesome stylistic addition — and in their in-ring "Raw" debut, Bronco Nima and Lucian Price were excellent Monday night against The Usos and Solo Sikoa. These guys are being booked as seriously strong performers, and they delivered in every aspect tonight.It was a fantastic main-event match, even if it had its holes, ending via the expected shenanigans.JAIDA PARKER TAKES OUT THE USOS!!! pic.twitter.com/qhBnlVGPXh— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 We labeled the finish as a no-contest, but realistically, the match straight-up never ended. They could still be fighting it out off-camera for all we know.All jokes aside, Parker removed the referee from the ring to break up Sikoa's pin on Royce Keys, and another simply never showed up. You know, like they always do in WWE. There's no way to justify this other than all the other referees were scared backstage, along with WWE staff, as indicated by Adam Pearce's conversation with said ref earlier in the night.GM Adam Pearce is doing everything in his power to keep CONTROL over tonight's main event! 👀@ScrapDaddyAP pic.twitter.com/6Bc49F0RE9— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 That's pretty good logic. But it again highlights how absurd it is to book literal kayfabe criminals in a match after they attempted to murder someone two weeks ago. Like, we know that 946 do not play by the rules, so why do they even care about getting DQ'd? (Until they don’t, anyway.) Some of those aspects really worked for the match though, as it was essentially a tornado tag match to start, before everyone got in their corners.(Again, I don't know why any of them would have waited in the corners under these circumstances, but, hey, wrestling!)So, with all of that in mind, this was a great main event, but it feels unfair to give it a star rating. It realistically shouldn't even have been advertised as a match. Nonetheless, we'll probably see Fatu and Naomi return before Survivor Series: WarGames to set up the five-on-five match, while Roman Reigns chills back home, not giving a single care in the world about these gang wars his family has gotten tied up in.This group is SCARY!! WHO can stop 946?? 😳 pic.twitter.com/tDhDMst8rF— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑Chad Gable is making a serious late push for Wrestler of the Year after delivering another flawless match with Rey Fenix tonight. Massive credit to Fenix, too, because he was exceptional. It wasn't a surprise, as we know what both men can do and have seen them go at it before, but this was next level. Every sequence was performed to perfection, and in the closing stretch, Fenix playing into his ankle damage off several ankle lock attempts was cinema.This was easily one of Gable's multiple Match of the Year candidates. It makes you wonder who could possibly be positioned to beat this guy when he looks so great in the ring like this.GABLE RETAINS!! 👏 @WWEGableThat was an INSTANT CLASSIC! pic.twitter.com/tWkrFhKuow— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 Champion vs. champion seasonThere's a lot wrong with the women's division as a collective unit right now. We won't get into every detail, but specifically, let's start with the upcoming Crown Jewel match on Nov. 7, which pits WWE’s two world champions against each other.WWE already announced it will be Reigns vs. Sami Zayn and Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green this year. The latter showed up on "Raw" tonight and cut a solid promo against The Judgment Day, leading to a match against Roxanne Perez."Dominik Mysterio's placeholder girlfriend" 🤯Shots FIRED by @ImChelseaGreen! pic.twitter.com/Rn58JwKn1Z— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 There was a time when I really loved the champion vs. champion matches, and they can still be incredibly cool, fun, you name it. But it would be nice if they meant something. And I mean anything. Give the winner more than a goofy single-match trophy. Let the champion have some type of advantage for their following title defense. Anything. I know champions hand out title shots on the regular these days, but there should be a clear reason to care about these matches beyond them being the wrestling version of an all-star game.As for Green vs. Perez, Green lost to typical Judgment Day shenanigans. All the nonsense aside, it's absurd for the Women's Champion to keep losing like this. But there’s still a way to make all this work beautifully … and I'm going to hold out hope.THE PRODIGY 👊@roxanne_wwe has PINNED the WWE Women's Champion! pic.twitter.com/7KRiYv7WVy— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 Fantasy Booking of the NightPerez losing her Money in the Bank match is a miss no matter how you slice it. But after her win tonight, she requested a title shot against Green. So, Perez dethrones Green, then we get the Judgment Day implosion and Perez vs. Morgan as champions?It might not work as well as a cash-in would, but it could be fun. And it works in a very roundabout way with Tiffany Stratton holding the women's briefcase. To avenge her friend (Green), Stratton cashes in on either Morgan or Perez to take the title and head into WrestleMania as champion — where she'll defend against the 2027 Royal Rumble winner, Green.That sounds a lot better to me than having Stratton rinse and repeat her last cash-in in the Nia Jax angle, which is where everyone's minds went once she won Saturday’s ladder match. But it’s important to note that Morgan casually slipped in a line about Stratton being injured, so monitor that for legitimacy after she took some horrific tumbles at MITB.Don't MESS with IYO! 🔥@Iyo_SkyWWE pic.twitter.com/rWA6jaqrmi— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 Big Cass — without the "C"This company couldn't care less about Big Cass, because he has become the biggest jobber in town. (Literally.)Even in 2026, losing to Rey Mysterio isn't necessarily something to be ashamed of. But it was the way he lost in this one, which was via Dragon Lee interference.A little assist from Dragon Lee leads to the WIN for @reymysterio over Big Cass!! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/ogHyFkxGDB— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 Cass took a 619 and was rolled up embarrassingly. That came after he completely no-sold a 619 to the back of the dome, which should probably be a more effective finisher than the normal move.We've simply already reached a point where Cass can't be taken seriously.Lost in the shuffleBron Breakker, Oba Femi, Penta and Je'Von all just kind of existed tonight.The opening segment saw Penta celebrate his briefcase win before Evans joined him — only to be broken in half by a Breakker Spear. That was that. It felt wildly directionless for all three, but at least Penta teased a surprise cash-in. Circling back to fantasy booking, ideally, Crown Jewel is the perfect opportunity for an extremely fun cash-in. Imagine Penta running to the ring to choose between a beaten-down Zayn or a victorious Reigns for a rematch of their Mexico City classic.BRON BREAKS THE YOUNG OG 😱This man really is an ANIMAL! @bronbreakkerwwe pic.twitter.com/kVVFcZAbju— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 Elsewhere on "Raw," Femi went face-to-face with Paul Heyman, essentially to tell him off after getting heaped with praise for his Bronson Reed win.This felt like a prime moment to see Breakker again, but we didn't. And there's zero telling what Femi will do next as WWE stalls him all the way until an April world title coronation."I am an Oba Femi guy" 🤌@Obaofwwe knows EXACTLY who he is! pic.twitter.com/uIiKwmLvAU— WWE (@WWE) October 13, 2026 I give this "Raw" a crown score of: 8/10 👑WWE Raw full card results and match grades:The Usos (Jey Uso and Jimmy Uso) and Solo Sikoa vs. The 946 (Royce Keys, Bronco Nima and Lucian Price) ends in a no-contestIntercontinental Championship: Chad Gable (c) def. articles.title: Discovery Plus is getting more expensive
articles.summary: Discovery Plus is going up in price, with the cheapest ad-supported plan now costing $6.99 / month, and the ad-free tier priced at $11.99 / month.
articles.body: Discovery Plus is raising prices across its ad-free and ad-supported plans. Starting Tuesday, the ad-supported plan will go from $5.99 to $6.99 / month, while the ad-free tier will jump from $9.99 to $11.99 / month. The price hike comes just one week after Paramount closed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, which owned Discovery Plus and HBO Max. The combined companies, known as Skydance, plan to merge Paramount Plus and HBO Max into “a single service over time,” though it’s not clear whether Discovery Plus will remain a standalone streamer. Discovery Plus streams shows from networks like TLC, The Discovery Channel, HGTV, Food Network, and Investigation Discovery. Many shows from the platform are also included within an HBO Max subscription, such as 90 Day Fiancé, Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives, and Deadliest Catch. Discovery Plus last raised prices in January 2025. This latest Discovery Plus price increase will go into effect immediately for new subscribers, while existing ones will see the increase in their next billing statement on or after November 12th.

articles.title: Jeffries: Nothing to merit ‘extraordinary raid’ on Omar home
articles.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) on Monday doubled down on his opposition to the federal raid on Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D) home, which came just three weeks before Election Day. “Right-wing conspiracy theorists have been targeting Rep. Omar for about eight years,” Jeffries told reporters at a campaign event in New Hampshire, according…
articles.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) on Monday doubled down on his opposition to the federal raid on Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D) home, which came just three weeks before Election Day.

“Right-wing conspiracy theorists have been targeting Rep. Omar for about eight years,” Jeffries told reporters at a campaign event in New Hampshire, according to a video shared by C-SPAN .

“At this particular point in time, there’s nothing there relative to behavior that should merit this type of extraordinary raid, let alone inside of 30 days from the date of an election,” the Democratic leader continued.

Agents with Homeland Security Investigations — the investigative arm of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — searched the progressive lawmaker’s home in Washington, D.C., on Monday as part of an ongoing criminal investigation .

In a Monday statement shared on social media, Omar’s office condemned the raid as an “outrageous abuse of power” and a “weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies.”

“For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back,” the statement read. “Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid.

“The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong,” the statement continued. “No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies.”

Trump has repeatedly derided Omar and accused the Somali-born lawmaker without evidence of fraudulently obtaining U.S. citizenship.

His administration announced last year it was opening an investigation into allegations that Omar married her brother to obtain U.S. citizenship. The lawmaker has denied these accusations.

The president has also sought to tie Omar to an alleged widespread welfare fraud scheme that involved members of Minnesota’s Somali-born community.

Trump called the Democratic lawmaker “ totally crooked ” in comments to reporters on Monday.

“I think she’s a terrible person, but that’s really up to the DOJ [Department of Justice],” he said, adding, “I have nothing to do with it.”

articles.title: Legal group files Hatch Act complaint over Omar search
articles.summary: A watchdog group filed a Hatch Act complaint Tuesday against several federal agencies following the search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minn.) home. Democracy Defenders Fund called for an investigation the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and its secretary, Markwayne Mullin, Attorney General Todd Blanche, the Justice Department (DOJ) and Joseph Edlow, the director of U.S.…
articles.body:
A watchdog group filed a Hatch Act complaint Tuesday against several federal agencies following the search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minn.) home.

Democracy Defenders Fund called for an investigation the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and its secretary, Markwayne Mullin, Attorney General Todd Blanche, the Justice Department (DOJ) and Joseph Edlow, the director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. The group referred to the raid and its timing as “outrageous.”

“This unprecedented raid occurred a mere four days before general early voting begins in Minnesota and appears to be timed to influence voters in the upcoming midterm election,” the complaint states.

In a post on the social platform X , Democracy Defenders Fund co-founder and executive chair Norm Eisen described the search of Omar’s home as a “textbook” case of authorities using “criminal power to affect an election.” The nonprofit filed the complaint alongside former President George W. Bush’s chief ethics lawyer, Richard Painter

The post featured a letter to Charles Baldis, the U.S. Office of Special Counsel’s (OSC) special counsel, in which the group asks him to investigate the raid for any potential Hatch Act violations — naming Mullin, Edlow and Blanche, as well as any other DHS and DOJ employees that may have been involved.

The Hatch Act bans federal employees from taking part in political activity while on duty or on federal property.

On Monday morning , federal agents searched Omar’s home as part of an ongoing criminal investigation. Homeland Security Investigations agents carried out the search, a DOJ spokesperson told NewsNation, The Hill’s sister network.

“This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” the Justice Department said in the statement.

Omar blasted the raid on social media, referring to it as “political intimidation.”

“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” she wrote on X. “For ten years, [President] Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”

Omar is seeking reelection Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District, where she’s facing off against Republican John Nagel. Nonpartisan election forecaster Decision Desk HQ sees the district as a “safe” Democratic victory , with Omar leading Nagel by almost eight points as of Oct. 10.

articles.title: Omar on Vance saying DOJ is investigating her: ‘That man is delusional’
articles.summary: Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) called Vice President Vance “delusional” after he said the Department of Justice (DOJ) is investigating her for possible immigration fraud, a day after federal agents raided her home in Washington. “That is not something that is happening,” Omar told a reporter when asked about Vance’s comments. “That man is delusional.” The…
articles.body:
Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) called Vice President Vance “delusional” after he said the Department of Justice (DOJ) is investigating her for possible immigration fraud, a day after federal agents raided her home in Washington.

“That is not something that is happening,” Omar told a reporter when asked about Vance’s comments. “That man is delusional.”

The Minnesota Democrat also pushed back when asked if she believed the probe would uncover wrongdoing.

Vance told reporters Tuesday at Joint Base Andrews that he had no advance knowledge of the raid.

In an interview with Fox News Digital later Tuesday, the vice president said the Trump administration would allow the DOJ to investigate Omar without political interference, but he said legal action could follow if investigators uncovered evidence of immigration fraud.

“We’re going to let the investigation unfold,” he added.

The probe stemmed from past allegations raised by GOP figures that Omar married her brother in order to obtain U.S. citizenship.

Vance in May said, “You read the things about Ilhan Omar … who she married and whether she didn’t marry this person or that person. It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody’s entitled to equal justice under the law.”

Omar has denied the allegations , which have circulated for roughly a decade now, and called the claims politically motivated.

White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed last month that a criminal investigation into the progressive lawmaker’s immigration history will take place in light of the allegations.

On Monday, federal agents with Homeland Security Investigations searched Omar’s home using a court-authorized search warrant. She has condemned the raid, accusing President Trump of targeting his political adversaries and describing the search as an intimidation tactic.

“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” she wrote on the social platform X . “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns.”

She continued, “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”

The Democrat has repeatedly sparred with Trump, with tensions rising in particular after the president went after Somali people in connection to a widespread fraud scandal in Minnesota.

Trump has attacked Somali refugees numerous times and has called Omar, a Somali native, “garbage.”

articles.title: Netflix is laying off around 1,000 employees
articles.summary: In its largest round of layoffs yet Netflix is cutting six percent of its workforce, or around 1,000 jobs, in an attempt to further drive growth.
articles.body: Following a report last week that Netflix was planning to lay off five percent of the company, today the streamer’s co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters announced in an email that it would actually be laying off six percent of its workforce, or around 1,000 employees, according to Variety, which obtained a copy of the memo. That makes this Netflix’s largest round of layoffs so far, following the company cutting 150 jobs in May 2022, and an additional 300 in June 2022 in an attempt to reduce costs following slower revenue growth. Today’s layoffs will mostly affect staff in Netflix’s product, technology, human resources, and legal teams, according to today’s memo. “Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” said the CEOs. “We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.” Netflix’s revenue increased to $45.2 billion in 2025 while its net income increase to $11 billion from 325 million subscribers. From 2024 to 2025 the streamer’s advertising business also more than doubled its revenue to $1.5 billion as a result of continued growth of its $7.99 per month ad-supported plan that had over 9.4 million subscribers as of May 2025.

articles.title: ‘I’ve been in your shoes’: Former Netflix employee Omar Sealey offers support as streaming giant cuts off 6% of workforce, laying off roughly 1,000 employees globally
articles.summary: Netflix is letting go of around 1,000 people worldwide, which is about 6% of its global workforce.
articles.body: Netflix is letting go of around 1,000 people worldwide, which is about 6% of its global workforce. For a lot of people, this means waking up to huge uncertainty: the end of plans, routines, and maybe security they've known for years. Not surprisingly, the anxiety and the sting of losing a job can be overwhelming.However, one former Netflix employee, Omar Sealey, isn’t just watching from the sidelines. He’s reaching out, making it clear that life and careers go on, even after bad news like this.Omar Sealey’s message on LinkedIn: What he saidSealey’s message on LinkedIn stands out because he’s not another outsider offering empty words. He’s been through the same thing. “I’ve been in your shoes,” he wrote, speaking directly to people who, just days ago, were part of the world’s biggest streaming company.In his post, Sealey wrote, “To everyone impacted by todays layoffs at Netflix, my heart goes out to you,” adding, “As a Netflix alum who has also experienced being laid off, I know firsthand how difficult this moment can be. The uncertainty, emotions, and questions about whats next are real. But I also know this: A layoff doesnt define your talent, your worth, or your future.”“Netflix is home to some of the most talented people Ive ever worked with, and I know incredible opportunities lie ahead for many of youIf theres anything I can do to help, please reach out,” Sealey wrote, “If youre a Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer, or Data Scientist, please DM me directly. Id love to explore opportunities and see if we can find a great fit for you.”Why is Netflix laying off 1,000 employees?According to Reuters and the Associated Press, Netflix announced plans on October 14 to cut around 6% of its global workforce, making this its largest round of layoffs since 2022. The company had approximately 16,000 full-time employees at the end of 2025. Of the departments hit hardest, product, technology, legal, and human resources teams are facing some of the deepest cuts. That means a wave of highly skilled engineers, analysts, and data experts are suddenly back on the hunt for work, often with little warning.But what exactly is behind these layoffs? Netflix is still making money: just this past quarter, the company pulled in $3.4 billion in profit on $12.56 billion in revenue, per AP News. However, as competition is heating up, with rivals like Disney+, YouTube, and even TikTok capturing attention (and dollars), the company is worried about the future.Per Reuters, the co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters told staff the business remains on track, but also stressed a need for “discipline” in how they manage teams. The uncomfortable truth is that, even in wildly successful companies, nobody’s job is ever 100% safe if business priorities shift.Omar Sealey: Who is he?For the unversed, Sealey is a Netflix alumnus who, not so long ago, got the same rough news himself. Instead of offering platitudes, he’s telling people what they truly need to hear: losing a job doesn’t erase your talent or potential. He’s not broadcasting a generic “good luck,” but genuinely trying to clear paths for those who are suddenly at a crossroads. However, his approach also says something bigger: sometimes, the most valuable help comes from inside your own community.It’s important to note that Sealey isn’t promising jobs, but sometimes, what you really need is a foot in the door or a frank conversation with someone who gets it. It’s one thing to scroll through endless job postings; quite another to have a real person vouch for your skills or point you in the right direction.As former Netflix employees take stock and plan their next moves, Sealey’s voice is a reminder: closing one door can open others, especially if you’re willing to reach out and let a community help you find them.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.summary: Federal authorities seized Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minn.) phone and issued subpoenas to some of her relatives as part of an ongoing criminal investigation. The subpoenas were issued as part of a federal grand jury probe of alleged fraud involving Omar’s immigration paperwork, The Associated Press reported, citing a person familiar with the matter who spoke…
articles.body:
Federal authorities seized Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minn.) phone and issued subpoenas to some of her relatives as part of an ongoing criminal investigation .

The subpoenas were issued as part of a federal grand jury probe of alleged fraud involving Omar’s immigration paperwork, The Associated Press reported , citing a person familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Sahra Noor, the Minnesota Democrat’s sister, and at least one other family member received a subpoena, according to The New York Times .

On Monday, agents with Homeland Security Investigations — the investigative arm of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — searched Omar’s home in Washington, D.C. The investigation comes roughly a month after White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed a federal criminal investigation involving Omar.

In a statement on the social platform X , the progressive lawmaker called the investigation “political intimidation.” She argued it was an effort by the Trump administration to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.

“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she wrote Monday. “I will not be silenced.”

Omar, who received her citizenship in 2000, came to the U.S. as a child with her family from Somalia as they sought asylum during the country’s civil war, which cause widespread displacement.

Trump and GOP lawmakers have made several claims against Omar in the past over her immigration status and accused her of fraud. The lawmaker has repeatedly denied all allegations.

The Justice Department does not typically take major action against candidates in the 60 days preceding an election. The midterms are less than three weeks away, and Omar is running for reelection.

articles.title: UK may make viewers pay to watch Netflix, Amazon, Disney Plus, YouTube and other streaming platforms; here's what proposed 'YouTube tax' is
articles.summary: Watching YouTube in the UK could soon come with a bill.
articles.body: Watching YouTube in the UK could soon come with a bill. The British government is reportedly preparing to extend the BBC licence fee, the £180 yearly charge households pay to watch live TV, to cover streaming platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney Plus and YouTube.The plan is expected to be part of a government white paper on renewing the BBC's royal charter, due before Christmas. It has already picked up an unofficial nickname, the "YouTube tax", since YouTube is Britain's biggest online video platform with around 55 million users and a 79% reach in the market.At present, the licence fee applies to anyone watching live TV on any device, or using BBC iPlayer. On-demand viewing on other services is exempt, so a household that only streams Netflix or YouTube pays nothing. A senior government source said people are using these platforms to dodge the fee, and called it unfair that viewers can watch TV content without paying for it.Streaming has become the easiest way around the BBC licence feeThe numbers show why the government is moving now. Around 539,000 fewer TV licences were in force in the year to March 31, 2026, and the total has dropped by roughly two million over five years. The BBC collects about £3.8 billion to £3.9 billion from the fee, yet still posted an operating deficit of £121 million for 2025/26.Bringing streaming under the fee could add an estimated 3 to 4 million paying households. That money, however, is not meant to fill the BBC's budget gaps. It is expected to fund local journalism and efforts against misinformation, which the source linked to the rise of parties such as Reform UK.The BBC has been asking for reform too. Director-general Matt Brittin has called the current model outdated and said BBC content should be on Netflix, YouTube, TikTok and Spotify. The broadcaster also plans to bring its news channel to YouTube.No final decision on the YouTube tax has been made yetThe Department for Culture, Media and Sport, led by Lisa Nandy, said it is weighing a range of options for the licence fee and that nothing has been decided.Earlier this month, a cross-party committee of MPs recommended that the fee should no longer be tied to live TV or a television set. It also suggested the cost could come down if more people pay. About 94% of people use the BBC every month, but only 80% of households hold a licence.Existing concessions, including free licences for over-75s on pension credit and a 50% discount for visually impaired viewers, are part of the current system. How a streaming-era fee would be collected, and whether platforms or households would foot the bill, is still unclear.The current charter expires in December 2027, so British viewers should know well before then whether their YouTube habit comes with a price.You use AI every day. articles.body: The ALCS continues Friday with the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians in Game 4 at Progressive Field. When the game actually begins has yet to be determined.Less than an hour before first pitch was scheduled, MLB announced the game would be indefinitely delayed. Rain has been pouring in Cleveland for much of the evening, and it's unclear when it will let up.The Guardians took a 2-1 series lead on Thursday with a 3-2 win over the Rays. A two-run homer from Petey Halpin off Griffin Jax put Cleveland on top. The two teams are playing to see who meets the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series.In Game 4, the Rays will start right-hander Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10 ERA) as they look to even the series. Martinez last pitched against the New York Yankees in Game 3 of the ALDS, striking out three while allowing 5 hits, 2 earned runs and 1 walk over 3 2/3 innings.Right-hander Shawn Armstrong (0-0, 4.58 ERA) will open for the Guardians against his former team, making his first career postseason start after appearing in 131 games for Tampa Bay over four seasons. Armstrong struck out one and allowed one hit over 1 2/3 innings of relief against the Rays in Game 2, and Cleveland is expected to lean on its bullpen behind him.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Guardians host the Rays in Game 4 of the ALCS, airing on TBS and truTV.

articles.title: It’s a dream week for tech docs
articles.summary: Apple’s HomeView, Musk, You Can See Everything, the Xbox Controller Nano, and more in this week’s Installer newsletter.
articles.body: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 148, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, hope you’re enjoying all your pumpkin-flavored everything, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.) This week, I’ve been reading about Marc Andreessen and the future of math and Mike Tomlin and Citizens United, reminiscing about the heyday of MySpace, sending this article to everyone as an apology for my bad texting, listening to the Pet Shop Boys’ new Alan Turing album and Dwarkesh Patel’s thoughts on AI, barely keeping myself from preordering an iPhone Duo, asking a lot of questions about that “flying” Tesla Roadster, and endlessly shopping for tripods to hold my phone for social videos. I have thought way too much about tripods this week. I also have for you a couple of huge new tech docs and a whole bunch of gadgets worth a look. Gadget season, baby! Let’s go. (As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you watching / reading / listening to / playing / throwing in the trunk this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.) The Drop * You Can See Everything. I can’t remember the last time I was so excited about a documentary (especially a three-hour one). The pairing of Elizabeth Holmes and Nathan Fielder, the shocking level of access, the incredible meta-ness of the whole project. I’ll be seeing this the first minute I can. Oh, and after you watch the doc, watch Josh Johnson’s hourlong set on all things Elizabeth Holmes. Glorious. * Musk. And here’s four more hours of tech doc! The reviews here are also spectacular, and even if you’ve been following the news the last decade or so, I suspect seeing it all in a row at once is going to be an experience. * The Apple HomeView. I keep staring at the buy button on this new $299 home hub. I’m not sure what I need it for, really — my very basic smart home is working just fine — but there’s something almost old-school about the idea of this as a sort of family computer. I’m certainly in the market for fewer reasons to look at my phone. * The new Siri Remote. I cannot in good conscience recommend a $300 Apple TV, but I can totally tell you to drop $60 on the new Find My-enabled remote! I mean, wait until you lose your existing one first. But you will. These remotes are impossible. * The Fairphone Fairbuds 2. I’ve come to like both Fairphone’s minimalist aesthetic and its emphasis on repairability, and the fact that it gets both into a lighter, smaller, longer-lasting, cheaper-than-AirPods package is pretty exciting. * The Xbox Nano Controller. Look at this little guy! A pocket-sized game controller comes in handy more often than you think (makes the waiting room a lot more fun), and this one has all the buttons you’d expect for Xbox and other games. If the battery life is good, this one’s gonna be a winner. * The Fitbit Edge. I’ve been using a Fitbit Air for a while, and I like it a lot, but I do miss having a fitness tracker that also told me the time. This one does that, plus a little more workout and biometric tracking. It’s not the handsomest wristwear I’ve ever seen, but it is very Fitbit. * The CMF Speaker S. I am a sucker for a cool Bluetooth speaker, and these futuristic milk carton-looking devices are fabulous. I bought one of the small ones immediately, and I’m already debating a second to build out the stereo pair. More companies should make speakers that look good! * E Ink Kaleido 4. This isn’t so much a specific gadget as it is good news for a whole category of gadgets: We have a new version of the color E Ink panel found in lots of devices, with promises of both better colors and better performance. Kaleido has let down a lot of devices, but I’m excited to see what comes of this. Screen share I’ve been reading Kevin Roose’s new book, The AGI Chronicles, this week, and I truly cannot recommend it enough. We sometimes make fun of Kevin for loving (and being loved by) AI too much, but this book is fabulously reported, has taught me a ton, and makes so many things about the AI industry make a lot more sense. And Kevin’s not done! He and (friend of Installer) Casey Newton are getting ready to launch their new show, Machine Gods, sometime next week. (If you were a Hard Fork fan, you’re gonna need to be listening to this one.) So I figured now was a good time to see how Kevin gets it all done — and whether he’s just Claude Code-d himself out of existence altogether. Have I even been texting with the real Kevin this week? WHO KNOWS. Here’s Kevin’s homescreen, plus some info on the apps he uses and why: [Image: The phone: iPhone 15 Pro (barely works, battery life is a joke, storage is full, but I’m holding out until I can preorder the Duo and become a new man). The wallpaper: A photo of my son fishing at the Russian River. The apps: Voice Memos, WhatsApp, Signal, Spotify, Google Maps, Safari, Day One, Brick, Stash, Superwhisper, Substack, Slack, Town, Apple Notes, Phone, Gmail, Messages. I’m a big dictation guy, I barely type anymore, and I use Superwhisper and Voice Memos for everything. I vibe-coded a Pocket replacement called Stash that is still a delight many months later. (Building your own apps is so fun!) And I’m running a swarm of AI agents that includes Skynet (my ChatGPT Dot, which I use mostly for personal tasks), Hootie (my work agent, which runs on an app called Town that Casey got me into), and Nancy (my Muse agent, who trades Kalshi on my behalf and has lost me $41 to date). I have a “red flags” app folder for social media and everything else I know is rotting my brain, a “green flags” folder for things that feel vaguely enriching, and an AI folder for all of my silly little bots. I also asked Kevin to share a few things he’s into right now. Here’s what he sent back: * I’m hopelessly addicted to Balatro, a poker roguelike game that Casey got me into. (I will never forgive him for this.) * We’re starting a new, YouTube-first podcast, so I’m watching a lot of popular YouTube shows like New Heights and Good Work to get ideas. * For fun, I usually stick with my hobby channels: Served (a tennis podcast hosted by Andy Roddick) and Roffle Lite (a Balatro streamer whose videos I sometimes fall asleep to), plus some stuff my son likes (Mark Rober, Bluey, Yoto stories) that I’ve also gotten into. * My favorite new app right now is Dreambeans, a truly demented Google Labs app that sends AI-generated illustrations of personalized suggestions for things to do every day. I’ll open it up and it’s like, “Today you could go birdwatching at Point Reyes” and it’s just a stylized cartoon of me looking at a heron through binoculars. I don’t think people know Dreambeans exists but I love it and am preemptively sad for 6 months from now when Google shuts it down. Crowdsourced Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky. “I’ve been using the markdown writing app, Em. I’m a longtime fan of iA Writer, but this plays so nicely with Ghost that my head has been turned.” — Chris “Just got my Bose Wired Earbuds, and I haven’t felt this excited and happy for a pair of earbuds since AirPods.” — Sai “I’ve been liking the app Shelf & Story for finding good books for my kids. Goodreads never quite cut it for me for that.” — Martha “Made by the founder of TV Time, Bingers is my new favorite media tracker. Lots of really neat features (like easily updating dates and automatically populating a watchlist). Still can be improved but it’s off to a great start and is the first thing I reach for over Letterboxd these days.” — pegasusisme “Just finished the most recent season of Jet Lag: The Game. Probably their best one yet. A fantastic jumping on point for anyone new to it.” — Shane “Carrie, as soon as my internet provider resolves the outage affecting my area.” — Kev “Doing my annual listen to Snow Crash — very much worth picking up in current times for anybody who has or hasn’t had the pleasure (Jonathan David is a PLEASURE to listen to).” — Jonathan “Still playing Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave. Completed my first path. Just in time for the expansion pass to get announced.” — Connor “I’ve been really hooked on small roguelikes, like the city-builder meets Balatro in Combolands and the same twist but billiards in Ultrapool. I’ve been playing them on the Steam Deck which is good with some mouse tweaks, but you need to be comfy with the trackpads.” — Scott Signing off I mentioned last week that I’ve switched notes app, this time to Capacities. Again. A few of you asked what finally clicked for me, and the answer is really simple: Capacities has this concept of “objects” instead of “notes,” which treats everything you save as a discrete type of thing. Images get treated and categorized one way; PDFs another; text notes another. Everything lives on its own, but is also organized by tags, dates, and however else you want. Getting this setup right is a lot of work, because you have to create and tune each object the way you want, but I spent an afternoon watching football and entering metadata and suddenly I can find things in my notes app again. This system won’t be for everybody — even at its best it’s pretty fiddly — but if you do wind up mucking around in Capacities, stare long and hard at this page in the documentation first. It’ll help. See you next week!
